# Setup

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)
library(jsonlite)
library(here)
library(mclust)
library(broom)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(dendextend)
library(ggcorrplot)

# Avoid masking by plyr/etc.
suppressMessages({
  library(conflicted)
  conflicts_prefer(
    dplyr::filter, dplyr::select, dplyr::mutate, dplyr::summarise,
    dplyr::count, dplyr::arrange, dplyr::slice, dplyr::rename, purrr::map,
    here::here,
    .quiet = TRUE
  )
})

# Base data path
base_path <- here("..", "data")
```

# Shared helpers

Two versions (grid, free-sort) share the same downstream logic — only the position-field names differ.

```{r}
#Extract final placement positions from grid version
extract_final_placements <- function(row, x_field, y_field,
                                     source_col = "move_log") {

  raw <- row[[source_col]]
  if (is.na(raw) || raw == "[]") return(NULL)

  parsed <- tryCatch(fromJSON(raw), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(parsed) || !is.data.frame(parsed)) return(NULL)

  if (!all(c(x_field, y_field) %in% names(parsed))) return(NULL)

  img_col <- if ("image_name" %in% names(parsed)) "image_name"
             else if ("image" %in% names(parsed)) "image"
             else return(NULL)

  parsed$posX <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(parsed[[x_field]]))
  parsed$posY <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(parsed[[y_field]]))

  # Only relevant for move_log (history) — no-op for placements (already final)
  if ("timestamp" %in% names(parsed)) {
    parsed <- parsed %>%
      mutate(timestamp = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(timestamp))) %>%
      group_by(.data[[img_col]]) %>%
      arrange(timestamp) %>%
      slice_tail(n = 1) %>%
      ungroup()
  }

  parsed %>%
    transmute(
      participant_id = row$participant_id,
      block          = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(row$block)),
      trial          = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(row$trial)),
      image_name     = .data[[img_col]],
      posX, posY
    )
}
```

```{r}
# Tag category / base_name / set from image filename.
# Image filenames look like "happy_1.png", "horse_2.jpg", etc.
tag_categories <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    mutate(
      image_stem = str_remove(image_name, "\\.[A-Za-z0-9]+$"),
      base_name  = str_remove(image_stem,  "_\\d+$"),
      set        = str_extract(image_stem, "\\d+$") %>% as.integer(),
      category   = case_when(
        str_detect(base_name,
                   "happy|sad|angry|fearful|surprise|disgust") ~ "emotions",
        str_detect(base_name,
                   "horse|lion|wolf|fish|squirrel|sheep|peacock|pigeon|fox|butterfly|ladybug|dolphin") ~ "animals",
        str_detect(base_name,
                   "tree|flower|grass|leaf|apple|broccoli|blueberry|acorn|cherry|cactus|cabbage|peanut") ~ "plants"
      )
    )
}
```

```{r}
# Normalize "p###" participant IDs from raw column.
normalize_pid <- function(x) {
  str_extract(as.character(x), "\\d+") %>%
    str_pad(width = 3, pad = "0") %>%
    str_c("p", .)
}

# Load all CSVs from a folder, normalize IDs.
load_folder <- function(folder) {
  list.files(folder, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE) %>%
    map_dfr(~ read_csv(.x, col_types = cols(.default = "c"))) %>%
    mutate(participant_id = normalize_pid(participant_id))
}

# Build final_placements.
build_placements <- function(folder, trial_type_label, x_field, y_field,
                             source_col = "move_log") {
  all_data <- load_folder(folder)

  trials <- all_data %>%
    filter(trial_type == trial_type_label,
           !is.na(block), block != "null")

  if (nrow(trials) == 0) {
    stop("No rows matched trial_type == '", trial_type_label,
         "'. trial_type values present: ",
         paste(unique(all_data$trial_type), collapse = ", "))
  }

  out <- trials %>%
    split(seq_len(nrow(.))) %>%
    map_dfr(~ extract_final_placements(.x, x_field, y_field, source_col))

  if (nrow(out) == 0) {
    stop("Extraction returned 0 placements from '", source_col, "'. ",
         "Check x_field/y_field ('", x_field, "', '", y_field,
         "') against the JSON keys in that column.")
  }

  out %>%
    mutate(trial = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(trial))) %>%
    filter(!is.na(trial), trial > 0) %>%
    tag_categories()
}
```

```{r}
# Add age_group label from an `age` column.
# Use after joining age_df so you don't have to repeat the case_when each time.
add_age_group <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    mutate(age_group = case_when(
      age <  5 ~ "4",
      age <  6 ~ "5",
      age <  7 ~ "6",
      age <  8 ~ "7",
      age >= 8 ~ "8"
    ))
}
```

```{r}
# Pairwise-distance vector from a set of coords, sorted by base_name
compute_dist_vec <- function(df) {
  coords <- df %>%
    arrange(base_name) %>%
    select(posX, posY) %>%
    as.matrix()
  as.vector(dist(coords))
}
```

```{r}
# Test-retest consistency per (participant, category).
#
# For each trial, average duplicate-emotion picture positions to one
# point per concept (no-op for animal/plant since they have 1 pic/concept).
# Then correlate trial 1 vs trial 2 distance vectors.
#
# Returns one row per (participant_id, category) with column `consistency`.
compute_consistency <- function(final_placements) {

  trial_positions <- final_placements %>%
    group_by(participant_id, category, trial, base_name) %>%
    summarise(posX = mean(posX), posY = mean(posY), .groups = "drop")

  trial_dist <- trial_positions %>%
    group_by(participant_id, category, trial) %>%
    nest() %>%
    mutate(dist_vec = map(data, compute_dist_vec)) %>%
    select(-data)

  trial_dist %>%
    group_by(participant_id, category) %>%
    summarise(
      consistency = if (length(dist_vec) < 2) NA_real_
                    else cor(dist_vec[[1]], dist_vec[[2]],
                             use = "complete.obs"),
      n_trials    = length(dist_vec),
      .groups     = "drop"
    )
}
```

```{r}
# Emotions-only: within-trial duplicate clustering.
# Within each emotion trial, correlate set-1 vs set-2 distance vectors,
# then average across the participant's emotion trials.
compute_within_trial <- function(final_placements) {
  final_placements %>%
    filter(category == "emotions") %>%
    group_by(participant_id, trial, set) %>%
    nest() %>%
    mutate(dist_vec = map(data, compute_dist_vec)) %>%
    select(-data) %>%
    group_by(participant_id, trial) %>%
    summarise(
      within_cor = if (length(dist_vec) < 2) NA_real_
                   else cor(dist_vec[[1]], dist_vec[[2]],
                            use = "complete.obs"),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    group_by(participant_id) %>%
    summarise(
      within_trial_consistency = mean(within_cor, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_trials = sum(!is.na(within_cor)),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}
```

```{r}
# Cluster the concepts in one trial, return cluster labels in base_name order.
cluster_trial <- function(df, k) {
  coords <- df %>% arrange(base_name) %>% select(posX, posY) %>% as.matrix()
  hc <- hclust(dist(coords), method = "ward.D2")
  cutree(hc, k = k)
}

# Cluster-based consistency: ARI between trial 1 and trial 2 cluster labels.
compute_cluster_consistency <- function(final_placements, k = 3) {

  trial_positions <- final_placements %>%
    group_by(participant_id, category, trial, base_name) %>%
    summarise(posX = mean(posX), posY = mean(posY), .groups = "drop")

  trial_clusters <- trial_positions %>%
    group_by(participant_id, category, trial) %>%
    nest() %>%
    mutate(cluster = map(data, ~ cluster_trial(.x, k = k))) %>%
    select(-data)

  trial_clusters %>%
    group_by(participant_id, category) %>%
    summarise(
      cluster_consistency = if (length(cluster) < 2) NA_real_
                            else mclust::adjustedRandIndex(cluster[[1]],
                                                          cluster[[2]]),
      n_trials = length(cluster),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}
```

# Grid version

```{r}
#| message: false
# Grid cell size in pixels (from the experiment: CELL_SIZE = 104, square cells).
GRID_CELL_SIZE <- 104

final_placements_grid <- build_placements(
  folder           = file.path(base_path, "grid_sort"),
  trial_type_label = "emotion-grid",
  x_field          = "grid_col",
  y_field          = "grid_row"
) %>%
  # Convert grid_col/grid_row to pixel cell-centers, matching the posX/posY
  # recorded in the data (posX = 104*col + 8, posY = 104*row). We compute from
  # grid_col/grid_row because every grid file has those, whereas only some
  # versions store posX/posY directly; the values are identical either way.
  mutate(
    posX = posX * GRID_CELL_SIZE + 8,
    posY = posY * GRID_CELL_SIZE
  )
```

```{r}
# Sanity check: each participant × category should have 2 trials,
# and within each trial each base_name should appear the expected # of times.
final_placements_grid %>%
  group_by(participant_id, category, trial) %>%
  summarise(n_concepts = n_distinct(base_name),
            n_images   = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  count(category, n_concepts, n_images)
```

```{r}
write_csv(final_placements_grid, "final_placements_grid.csv")
```

# Compare to predefined sub-categories

```{r}
# Predefine sub-categories within each domain.
subcategories <- tribble(
  ~base_name,   ~subcategory,
  # Emotions: valence
  "happy",      "positive",   "surprise", "positive",
  "sad",        "negative",   "angry",    "negative",
  "fearful",    "negative",   "disgust",  "negative",
  # Animals: 
  "horse",      "herbivore", "lion",    "carnivore",
  "wolf",       "carnivore", "squirrel","herbivore",
  "sheep",      "herbivore", "fox",     "carnivore",
  "dolphin",    "aquatic",     "fish",    "aquatic",
  "peacock",    "bird",        "pigeon",  "bird",
  "butterfly",  "insect",      "ladybug", "insect",
  # Plants: 
  "apple",      "fruit",   "blueberry", "fruit",
  "cherry",     "fruit",   "peanut",    "nut",
  "broccoli",   "vegetable",   "cabbage",   "vegetable",
  "tree",       "nature","flower",    "nature",
  "grass",      "nature","leaf",      "nature",
  "acorn",      "nut","cactus",    "nature"
)

compute_cat_org <- function(final_placements, subcategories) {

  positions <- final_placements %>%
    group_by(participant_id, category, trial, base_name) %>%
    summarise(posX = mean(posX), posY = mean(posY), .groups = "drop") %>%
    left_join(subcategories, by = "base_name")

  ratio_one_trial <- function(df) {
    if (n_distinct(df$subcategory) < 2) return(NA_real_)
    d <- as.matrix(dist(as.matrix(df %>% select(posX, posY))))
    same <- outer(df$subcategory, df$subcategory, "==")
    diag(same) <- NA
    within  <- mean(d[same == TRUE],  na.rm = TRUE)
    between <- mean(d[same == FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
    between / within
  }

  positions %>%
    group_by(participant_id, category, trial) %>%
    nest() %>%
    mutate(cat_org = map_dbl(data, ratio_one_trial)) %>%
    select(-data) %>%
    group_by(participant_id, category) %>%
    summarise(cat_org = mean(cat_org, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
}
```

```{r}

  left_join(age_df, by = "participant_id") %>%

  )
```

```{r}
participant_pairwise_long <- function(fp, normalize = FALSE) {
  out <- fp %>%
    group_by(participant_id, category, trial, base_name) %>%
    summarise(posX = mean(posX), posY = mean(posY), .groups = "drop") %>%
    group_by(participant_id, category, trial) %>%
    group_modify(function(d, key) {
      d <- d %>% arrange(base_name)
      m <- as.matrix(dist(as.matrix(d[, c("posX", "posY")])))
      dimnames(m) <- list(d$base_name, d$base_name)
      as.data.frame(as.table(m)) %>%
        transmute(item1 = as.character(Var1),
                  item2 = as.character(Var2),
                  dist  = Freq) %>%
        filter(item1 < item2)
    }) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    group_by(participant_id, category, item1, item2) %>%
    summarise(dist = mean(dist), .groups = "drop")   # average across trials

  if (normalize) {
    out <- out %>%
      group_by(participant_id, category) %>%
      mutate(dist = dist / mean(dist, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
      ungroup()
  }
  out
}

# Average across subjects within each (category, age_group) -> long format.
avg_dist_long_byGroup <- function(fp, age_df, normalize = FALSE) {
  participant_pairwise_long(fp, normalize = normalize) %>%
    left_join(age_df, by = "participant_id") %>%
    add_age_group() %>%
    filter(!is.na(age_group)) %>%
    group_by(category, age_group, item1, item2) %>%
    summarise(avg_dist = mean(dist), .groups = "drop")
}

# Long -> dist object (reimplements the paper's long_to_dist).
long_to_dist <- function(d) {
  items <- sort(unique(c(d$item1, d$item2)))
  m <- matrix(0, length(items), length(items), dimnames = list(items, items))
  m[cbind(match(d$item1, items), match(d$item2, items))] <- d$avg_dist
  m[cbind(match(d$item2, items), match(d$item1, items))] <- d$avg_dist
  as.dist(m)
}
```

```{r}
# Build cluster objects per (version, category, age_group).
build_clusters <- function(fp, age_df, version_label, normalize = FALSE) {
  avg_dist_long_byGroup(fp, age_df, normalize = normalize) %>%
    group_by(category, age_group) %>%
    nest() %>%
    mutate(
      n_concepts = map_int(data, ~ length(unique(c(.x$item1, .x$item2)))),
      dist_obj   = map(data, long_to_dist),
      cluster    = map(dist_obj, ~ hclust(.x, method = "ward.D2")),
      dend       = map(cluster, as.dendrogram),
      cut3       = map(cluster, ~ cutree(.x, k = 3))
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(version = version_label)
}

clusters_all <- bind_rows(
  build_clusters(final_placements_grid, age_df, "grid", normalize = TRUE),
  build_clusters(final_placements_free, age_df, "free", normalize = TRUE)
)

clusters_all %>% select(version, category, age_group, n_concepts)
```

```{r}
# Dendrograms: one panel per (category x age group) per version.
plot_dendros <- function(clusters_df, version_label, k = 4) {
  sub <- clusters_df %>% 
    filter(version == version_label) %>%
    arrange(category, age_group)
  
  if (nrow(sub) == 0) return(invisible(NULL))
  
  op <- par(mfrow = c(3, 3), mar = c(2, 2, 3, 6))
  on.exit(par(op))
  
  pwalk(
    list(sub$cluster, sub$category, sub$age_group),
    function(clst, cat, ag) {
      dend <- as.dendrogram(clst)
      
      dend <- dend %>%
        set("branches_lwd", 2) %>%
        set("branches_k_color", value = c("#5102A3", "#B43359", "#F1731D", "#F6D442"), k = k)
      
      plot(
        dend,
        horiz = TRUE,
        main = paste0(version_label, ": ", cat, ", ", ag)
      )
    }
  )
}
plot_dendros(clusters_all, "grid")
plot_dendros(clusters_all, "free")
```

```{r}
# Correlation between age groups (cophenetic, like cor.dendlist),
# one matrix per (version, category).
age_group_dend_cor <- function(clusters_df, version_label, cat) {
  sub <- clusters_df %>%
    filter(version == version_label, category == cat) %>%
    arrange(age_group)
  if (nrow(sub) < 2) return(NULL)
  dl <- do.call(dendlist, setNames(sub$dend, as.character(sub$age_group)))
  cor.dendlist(dl)
}

plot_dend_cor <- function(clusters_df, version_label, cat) {
  m <- tryCatch(age_group_dend_cor(clusters_df, version_label, cat),
                error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(m)) {
    message(version_label, " / ", cat,
            ": skipped (mismatched leaves or <2 age groups)")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  print(
    ggcorrplot(m, type = "lower", lab = TRUE, outline.color = "black",
               ggtheme = ggplot2::theme_void()) +
      ggtitle(paste0(version_label, " - ", cat))
  )
}

for (v in c("grid", "free"))
  for (cat in c("animals", "plants", "emotions"))
    plot_dend_cor(clusters_all, v, cat)
```

```{r}
participant_dist_vecs <- function(fp) {
  fp %>%
    group_by(participant_id, category, trial, base_name) %>%
    summarise(posX = mean(posX), posY = mean(posY), .groups = "drop") %>%
    group_by(participant_id, category, trial) %>%
    nest() %>%
    mutate(dvec = map(data, compute_dist_vec)) %>%
    select(-data) %>%
    group_by(participant_id, category) %>%
    summarise(dvec = list(reduce(dvec, `+`) / length(dvec)), .groups = "drop")
}

between_subject_consistency <- function(fp, age_df) {
  participant_dist_vecs(fp) %>%
    left_join(age_df, by = "participant_id") %>%
    add_age_group() %>%
    filter(!is.na(age_group)) %>%
    group_by(category, age_group) %>%
    summarise(
      between_consistency = {
        v <- dvec
        if (length(v) < 2) NA_real_
        else mean(combn(length(v), 2, function(ix)
          cor(v[[ix[1]]], v[[ix[2]]], use = "complete.obs")), na.rm = TRUE)
      },
      n = n(),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

between_subj_all <- bind_rows(
  between_subject_consistency(final_placements_grid, age_df) %>% mutate(version = "grid"),
  between_subject_consistency(final_placements_free, age_df) %>% mutate(version = "free")
)
between_subj_all
```

```{r}
between_subj_all %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = age_group, y = between_consistency, fill = category)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge2(preserve = "single")) +
  facet_wrap(~ version) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "animals" = "#0F728B",
      "emotions" =  "#29A099",
      "plants" = "#EDEF5c"
    )) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    x = "Age Group",
    y = "Between-subject consistency (mean pairwise r)",
    title = "Between-subject agreement by age group and category"
  )
```

# Comprehension Check

Practice trial 2 shows five food images with an a priori two-group structure (toast / bread / croissant vs chocolate / candy). We use it to ask whether the child understood that distance encodes relatedness.

**Criteria.** For each of four anchor items we look at its nearest neighbour:

| Anchor    | Acceptable nearest neighbour |
|-----------|------------------------------|
| chocolate | croissant, candy             |
| candy     | croissant, chocolate         |
| bread     | toast, croissant             |
| toast     | bread, croissant             |

Croissant counts as acceptable for all four anchors, since it is genuinely ambiguous between the two groups (a bread by form, a sweet pastry by taste).

-   **Level 1 (lenient)** — at least one of the four checks passes
-   **Level 2 (strict)** — all four checks pass

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: filter-setup
AGE_MIN        <- 4
AGE_MAX        <- 9      # exclusive
PRACTICE_TRIAL <- -2

GROUP_MAP <- c(toast = "bread", bread = "bread", croissant = "bread",
               chocolate = "sweet", candy = "sweet")

ACCEPTABLE <- list(
  chocolate = c("croissant", "candy"),
  candy     = c("croissant", "chocolate"),
  bread     = c("toast", "croissant"),
  toast     = c("bread", "croissant")
)

N_CHECKS <- length(ACCEPTABLE)
```

## Extract practice trial 2

`build_placements()` cannot be reused here: it filters out `block == "null"` and keeps only `trial > 0`, and practice trials have a null block and `trial == -2`.

```{r}
#| label: practice-extract
#| message: false
practice_placements <- load_folder(file.path(base_path, "free_sort")) %>%
  filter(trial_type == "emotion-grid") %>%
  split(seq_len(nrow(.))) %>%
  map_dfr(~ extract_final_placements(.x, "posX", "posY",
                                     source_col = "placements")) %>%
  mutate(trial = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(trial))) %>%
  filter(trial == PRACTICE_TRIAL) %>%
  mutate(
    image_stem = str_remove(image_name, "\\.[A-Za-z0-9]+$"),
    base_name  = str_remove(image_stem, "_\\d+$"),
    group      = unname(GROUP_MAP[base_name])
  )

stopifnot(nrow(practice_placements) > 0)

cat("Practice-2 rows:", nrow(practice_placements),
    "from", n_distinct(practice_placements$participant_id), "children\n")

# Every image should map to a group; NAs here mean GROUP_MAP needs fixing
practice_placements %>% count(base_name, group)
```

## Restrict to ages 4–8

```{r}
#| label: filter-restrict
pp <- practice_placements %>%
  filter(!is.na(group)) %>%
  inner_join(age_df %>% mutate(age_years = floor(age)), by = "participant_id") %>%
  filter(age_years >= AGE_MIN, age_years < AGE_MAX)

cat("Children in the 4-8 window:", n_distinct(pp$participant_id), "\n")

# Images per child (all should be 5)
pp %>% count(participant_id, name = "n_images") %>% count(n_images)
```

## Pairwise distances

`distance_norm` divides by each child's own mean pairwise distance, which controls for children who used only a small part of the canvas.

```{r}
#| label: filter-distances
pair_distances <- pp %>%
  select(participant_id, age, age_years, base_name, posX, posY) %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    d <- as.matrix(dist(cbind(.x$posX, .x$posY)))
    dimnames(d) <- list(.x$base_name, .x$base_name)
    as.data.frame(as.table(d)) %>%
      rename(item_a = Var1, item_b = Var2, distance = Freq) %>%
      filter(as.character(item_a) < as.character(item_b))
  }) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(pp %>% distinct(participant_id, age, age_years), by = "participant_id") %>%
  mutate(
    item_a    = as.character(item_a),
    item_b    = as.character(item_b),
    pair      = paste(item_a, item_b, sep = " - "),
    pair_type = case_when(
      GROUP_MAP[item_a] == "sweet" & GROUP_MAP[item_b] == "sweet" ~ "within sweets",
      GROUP_MAP[item_a] == "bread" & GROUP_MAP[item_b] == "bread" ~ "within breads",
      TRUE                                                        ~ "between groups"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  mutate(distance_norm = distance / mean(distance)) %>%
  ungroup()

head(pair_distances)
```

## Nearest neighbour of each anchor item

```{r}
#| label: filter-anchors
long_dist <- bind_rows(
  pair_distances %>% select(participant_id, from = item_a, to = item_b, distance),
  pair_distances %>% select(participant_id, from = item_b, to = item_a, distance)
)

anchor_ranks <- long_dist %>%
  filter(from %in% names(ACCEPTABLE)) %>%
  group_by(participant_id, from) %>%
  arrange(distance, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  summarise(
    nearest      = first(to),
    nearest_dist = round(first(distance), 1),
    second       = nth(to, 2),
    farthest     = last(to),
    n_tied_min   = sum(distance == min(distance)),
    .groups      = "drop"
  ) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(ok = nearest %in% ACCEPTABLE[[from]]) %>%
  ungroup()

if (any(anchor_ranks$n_tied_min > 1)) {
  warning(sum(anchor_ranks$n_tied_min > 1),
          " anchor(s) had tied nearest neighbours; the first was used.")
}

anchor_ranks
```

## Pass rate for each of the four checks

```{r}
#| label: filter-anchor-rates
anchor_ranks %>%
  group_by(anchor = from) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            n_ok   = sum(ok),
            pct_ok = round(100 * mean(ok), 1),
            .groups = "drop")
```

## Two levels

```{r}
#| label: filter-levels
levels_tbl <- anchor_ranks %>%
  select(participant_id, from, nearest, ok) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from  = from,
              values_from = c(nearest, ok),
              names_glue  = "{from}_{.value}") %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(n_ok = sum(c_across(ends_with("_ok")))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    pass_L1 = n_ok >= 1,          # at least one check
    pass_L2 = n_ok == N_CHECKS    # all four checks
  ) %>%
  left_join(pp %>% distinct(participant_id, age, age_years),
            by = "participant_id")

levels_tbl %>%
  summarise(
    n              = n(),
    mean_n_ok      = round(mean(n_ok), 2),
    L1_lenient_pct = round(100 * mean(pass_L1), 1),
    L2_strict_pct  = round(100 * mean(pass_L2), 1)
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: apply-comprehension-filter
MIN_CHECKS <- 3

kids_keep <- levels_tbl %>% filter(n_ok >= MIN_CHECKS) %>% pull(participant_id)

cat("Keeping", length(kids_keep), "of", nrow(levels_tbl),
    "children (>=", MIN_CHECKS, "of 4 checks)\n")

final_placements_free_f <- final_placements_free %>%
  filter(participant_id %in% kids_keep)

consistency_free_f <- consistency_all %>%
  filter(version == "free", participant_id %in% kids_keep)
```

## How many of the four checks each child passes

```{r}
#| label: filter-ncheck-dist
levels_tbl %>%
  count(n_ok, name = "n_children") %>%
  complete(n_ok = 0:N_CHECKS, fill = list(n_children = 0)) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n_children / sum(n_children), 1))
```

```{r}
#| label: filter-ncheck-cumulative
# Passing AT LEAST k of the four
tibble(at_least = 0:N_CHECKS) %>%
  mutate(
    n_children = map_int(at_least, ~ sum(levels_tbl$n_ok >= .x)),
    pct        = round(100 * n_children / nrow(levels_tbl), 1),
    level      = case_when(at_least == 1        ~ "L1 (lenient)",
                           at_least == N_CHECKS ~ "L2 (strict)",
                           TRUE                 ~ "")
  )
```

## Pass rates by age

If pass rates rise steeply with age, the criterion is partly measuring the developmental effect being studied.

```{r}
#| label: filter-pass-by-age
levels_tbl %>%
  group_by(age_years) %>%
  summarise(
    n          = n(),
    mean_n_ok  = round(mean(n_ok), 2),
    L1_lenient = round(100 * mean(pass_L1), 1),
    at_least_2 = round(100 * mean(n_ok >= 2), 1),
    at_least_3 = round(100 * mean(n_ok >= 3), 1),
    L2_strict  = round(100 * mean(pass_L2), 1),
    .groups    = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: filter-ncheck-by-age
# Full distribution of n_ok within each age (counts and row percentages)
levels_tbl %>%
  count(age_years, n_ok) %>%
  complete(age_years, n_ok = 0:N_CHECKS, fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
  group_by(age_years) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = n_ok, values_from = c(n, pct),
              names_glue = "n_ok{n_ok}_{.value}")
```

```{r}
#| label: filter-ncheck-plot
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
levels_tbl %>%
  count(age_years, n_ok) %>%
  group_by(age_years) %>%
  mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(age_years), y = pct, fill = factor(n_ok))) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "RdYlBu", name = "checks\npassed") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "How many of the four grouping checks children pass",
       x = "Age (years)", y = "% of children")
```

## Children who fail Level 1

These children passed **none** of the four checks — every anchor's nearest neighbour came from the other group.

```{r}
#| label: filter-failures
failures <- levels_tbl %>%
  filter(!pass_L1) %>%
  select(participant_id, age, age_years, n_ok, ends_with("_nearest")) %>%
  arrange(age)

cat("Failing Level 1 (0 of", N_CHECKS, "checks):", nrow(failures),
    "of", nrow(levels_tbl), "children\n\n")
failures
```

```{r}
#| label: filter-failures-detail
# Full distance profile for each failing child, nearest pair first.
# Worth eyeballing before excluding anyone.
if (nrow(failures) > 0) {
  pair_distances %>%
    semi_join(failures, by = "participant_id") %>%
    select(participant_id, age_years, pair, pair_type, distance) %>%
    mutate(distance = round(distance, 1)) %>%
    arrange(participant_id, distance) %>%
    print(n = Inf)
} else {
  cat("No children failed Level 1.\n")
}
```

## Children failing Level 2 only

Passed at least one check but not all four.

```{r}
#| label: filter-failures-l2
levels_tbl %>%
  filter(pass_L1, !pass_L2) %>%
  select(participant_id, age, age_years, n_ok,
         ends_with("_nearest"), ends_with("_ok")) %>%
  arrange(n_ok, age)
```

## Participants - graded passing rate

```{r}
#| label: filter-ids-by-ncheck
levels_tbl %>%
  arrange(n_ok, age) %>%
  group_by(n_ok) %>%
  summarise(
    n_children   = n(),
    participants = paste(participant_id, collapse = ", "),
    .groups      = "drop"
  ) %>%
  complete(n_ok = 0:N_CHECKS,
           fill = list(n_children = 0, participants = "—"))
```

## Sensitivity: age effect under each level

```{r}
#| label: filter-sensitivity
cons <- consistency_all %>%
  filter(version == "free") %>%
  semi_join(levels_tbl, by = "participant_id")

fit_age <- function(dat, label) {
  if (n_distinct(dat$participant_id) < 5) {
    return(tibble(sample = label, n_children = n_distinct(dat$participant_id),
                  slope = NA_real_, p_value = NA_real_, mean_cons = NA_real_))
  }
  m <- lm(consistency ~ age, data = dat)
  tibble(sample     = label,
         n_children = n_distinct(dat$participant_id),
         slope      = round(coef(m)[["age"]], 4),
         p_value    = round(summary(m)$coefficients["age", 4], 4),
         mean_cons  = round(mean(dat$consistency, na.rm = TRUE), 3))
}

keep_atleast <- function(k) {
  levels_tbl %>% filter(n_ok >= k) %>% pull(participant_id)
}

bind_rows(
  fit_age(cons, "no filter"),
  fit_age(cons %>% filter(participant_id %in% keep_atleast(1)), "L1: >=1 check"),
  fit_age(cons %>% filter(participant_id %in% keep_atleast(2)), ">=2 checks"),
  fit_age(cons %>% filter(participant_id %in% keep_atleast(3)), ">=3 checks"),
  fit_age(cons %>% filter(participant_id %in% keep_atleast(4)), "L2: all 4 checks")
)
```

## What each anchor's nearest neighbour actually was

Watch for croissant here: because it is acceptable for all four anchors, a child who parks it in the middle of everything can pass checks without having separated the two groups.

```{r}
#| label: dist-plot-nearest
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6
anchor_ranks %>%
  left_join(pp %>% distinct(participant_id, age_years), by = "participant_id") %>%
  count(age_years, from, nearest, ok) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = nearest, y = n, fill = ok)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_grid(from ~ age_years) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#2b8cbe", "FALSE" = "#d62728"),
                    name = "acceptable") +

  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
```

```{r}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A. Which picture set did each trial use?
#
# The model RDM must be built from the pictures the child actually saw. Two
# possibilities, and they need different handling:
#
#   sets_used == "1" in one trial and "2" in the other
#       -> each trial used a different picture set. Build one RDM per set and
#          average the two, matching what participant_dist_vecs() does to the
#          child data (distance computed within trial, then averaged).
#
#   sets_used == "1+2" within a trial
#       -> both pictures of each concept were on screen together (this is how
#          emotions works). Average the two exemplar embeddings, then compute
#          distances -- matching the group_by(..., base_name) %>% mean(posX)
#          step in your pipeline.
#
# Do not assume; the answer differs by category.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

set_structure <- bind_rows(
  final_placements_grid %>% mutate(version = "grid"),
  final_placements_free %>% mutate(version = "free")
) %>%
  group_by(version, participant_id, category, trial) %>%
  summarise(
    sets_used  = paste(sort(unique(set)), collapse = "+"),
    n_concepts = n_distinct(base_name),
    n_images   = n(),
    .groups    = "drop"
  )

cat("\n--- A. picture-set structure per trial ---\n")
set_structure %>%
  count(version, category, sets_used, n_concepts, n_images) %>%
  arrange(version, category) %>%
  print(n = Inf)

# Does a given category use a consistent scheme across children?
cat("\nCategories where children differ in which sets they saw per trial:\n")
set_structure %>%
  group_by(version, category, trial) %>%
  summarise(schemes = n_distinct(sets_used), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(schemes > 1) %>%
  print(n = Inf)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# B. Concept inventory -> input for 01_build_model_rdms.py
#
# Writing this out, rather than letting the Python script glob a stimulus
# folder, guarantees two things: the model sees exactly the images the children
# saw (not leftovers in the folder), and the concept strings are byte-identical
# to the base_name values R will sort on. Everything downstream depends on
# those two sets of strings agreeing.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

concept_inventory <- bind_rows(final_placements_grid, final_placements_free) %>%
  filter(!is.na(category)) %>%   # tag_categories() leaves NA for unmatched names
  distinct(category, base_name, set, image_name) %>%
  arrange(category, base_name, set)

# Any image whose base_name tag_categories() could not place. These would be
# silently dropped from every RDM, so look at them now.
unmatched <- bind_rows(final_placements_grid, final_placements_free) %>%
  filter(is.na(category)) %>%
  distinct(base_name, image_name)
if (nrow(unmatched)) {
  cat("\nImages with no category tag (fix tag_categories() if unexpected):\n")
  print(unmatched, n = Inf)
}

cat("\n--- B. concept inventory ---\n")
concept_inventory %>%
  group_by(category) %>%
  summarise(n_concepts = n_distinct(base_name),
            n_images   = n(),
            sets       = paste(sort(unique(set)), collapse = ", "),
            .groups    = "drop") %>%
  print()

# Every concept should have the same number of images. Rows here are problems.
cat("\nConcepts with an unusual number of images:\n")
concept_inventory %>%
  count(category, base_name, name = "n_img") %>%
  group_by(category) %>%
  filter(n_img != median(n_img)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  print(n = Inf)

write_csv(concept_inventory, "concept_inventory.csv")
cat("\nwrote concept_inventory.csv (", nrow(concept_inventory), "rows )\n")

# The exact concept list, in the order every RDM must use.
cat("\nConcepts in RDM order (sort(base_name)), per category:\n")
concept_lists <- concept_inventory %>%
  group_by(category) %>%
  summarise(concepts = paste(sort(unique(base_name)), collapse = ", "),
            .groups = "drop")
walk2(concept_lists$category, concept_lists$concepts,
      ~ cat("  ", .x, ": ", .y, "\n", sep = ""))


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# C. The reliability ceiling -- read this before trusting any model correlation
#
# A child's distance vector is a noisy measurement, and a noisy measurement
# cannot correlate with a noiseless model RDM above sqrt(its reliability).
#
# Two steps to get the right ceiling:
#
#   1. `consistency` is the test-retest r of a SINGLE trial. But
#      participant_dist_vecs() averages the two trials, and averaging lifts
#      reliability (Spearman-Brown): rel_avg = 2*r / (1 + r). At r = .15 that
#      is .26, not .15.
#   2. The ceiling is sqrt(rel_avg). At r = .15 that is .51, not .39.
#
# So the situation is better than the raw consistencies suggest -- but still
# low enough that the raw model correlations will be heavily attenuated.
#
# The real problem is for the age analysis: reliability itself rises with age,
# so a rising raw correlation is partly just children getting less noisy.
# Simulated at this design (66 pairs, reliability ramping .08 -> .42 across
# ages 4-8), a CONSTANT true balance produces a spurious slope of about
# +.04/year in the raw correlation. That is large enough to be mistaken for the
# result. 03_model_comparison.R handles it by switching DV and by partialling
# reliability out; compute the ceiling now so you know the scale of it.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

sb <- function(r) 2 * pmax(r, 0) / (1 + pmax(r, 0))   # Spearman-Brown, 2 trials

cat("\n--- C. max observable correlation, by category ---\n")
consistency_all %>%
  filter(!is.na(consistency)) %>%
  group_by(version, category) %>%
  summarise(mean_rtt = mean(consistency), n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(rel_trial_avg    = round(sb(mean_rtt), 3),
         max_observable_r = round(sqrt(sb(mean_rtt)), 3),
         mean_rtt         = round(mean_rtt, 3)) %>%
  print(n = Inf)

cat("\n--- C. the same ceiling, by age (this is the confound) ---\n")
consistency_all %>%
  filter(!is.na(consistency), !is.na(age_group)) %>%
  group_by(version, age_group) %>%
  summarise(mean_rtt = mean(consistency), n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(rel_trial_avg    = round(sb(mean_rtt), 3),
         max_observable_r = round(sqrt(sb(mean_rtt)), 3),
         mean_rtt         = round(mean_rtt, 3)) %>%
  print(n = Inf)

# Per-child reliability, saved for use as a covariate later. Computed from two
# trials over 66 pairs, so it is itself noisy -- good enough as a covariate,
# not good enough to divide by.
child_reliability <- consistency_all %>%
  filter(!is.na(consistency)) %>%
  select(version, participant_id, category, reliability = consistency)

write_csv(child_reliability, "child_reliability.csv")
cat("\nwrote child_reliability.csv\n")
```

```{r}
# =============================================================================
# 03_model_comparison.R
#
# Correlate children's arrangements with the reference RDMs from
# 01_build_model_rdms.py, and ask whether the perceptual/conceptual balance
# shifts with age.
#
# Needs, from kidsnet_pilot_analysis.qmd:
#   final_placements_grid / final_placements_free
#   age_df
#   compute_dist_vec()          (already in your file)
#   participant_dist_vecs()     (already in your file)
# and, from 01_build_model_rdms.py:
#   model_rdms_long.csv
#
# THE ONE THING THAT MATTERS MOST HERE
# ------------------------------------
# A noisy measurement cannot correlate with a noiseless model RDM above
# sqrt(its reliability), and your reliability RISES with age (free version:
# .034, .136, .297, .264, .332 from age 4 to 8). So a model correlation that
# rises with age is partly just children getting less noisy.
#
# Simulated at YOUR design and YOUR reliabilities (66 pairs, n = 110 per
# domain), with the true perceptual/conceptual balance held CONSTANT across
# age, the spurious age slope is:
#
#                                   all ages   ages 5-8   + reliability cov.
#   raw correlation with a model      +.045      +.027      +.036 / +.021
#   conceptual share (true = .80)     +.031      +.017      +.025 / +.014
#
# and the smallest slope this design can detect in the share is about
# .067/year (= .27 across ages 4-8). Three conclusions, in order of how much
# they change what you do:
#
#   1. DO NOT report a raw age slope as a finding. The artifact is as large as
#      a real effect would be.
#   2. The reliability covariate helps far less than you would hope -- about a
#      20% reduction -- because the covariate is itself estimated from two
#      trials and so under-corrects. It is worth including, but it is not a
#      fix, and an earlier version of this script overstated it.
#   3. Excluding the 4-year-olds does roughly twice as much as the covariate
#      (a 45% reduction). Their single-trial reliability of .034 means their
#      distance vectors carry almost no repeatable signal. Section 7 fits all
#      three versions so you can see the effect move.
#
# Why the share is better than the raw correlation at all: in the population,
# R-squared of y = t + e on any predictor set equals R-squared of t times the
# reliability, so BOTH unique shares scale by the same factor and it cancels in
# the ratio. What is left is finite-sample R-squared bias (~1/66 added to each
# share), which pulls the ratio toward .5.
#
# That shrinkage is large, so read observed shares as a LOWER BOUND on the true
# imbalance. Simulated at your reliabilities:
#
#     true share   observed, 66 pairs   observed, 15 pairs
#        0.20            0.37                 0.45
#        0.50            0.50                 0.50
#        0.80            0.64                 0.55
#
# A 15-pair domain (6 concepts, i.e. emotions) compresses so hard that the
# share is uninformative there. That is a reason not to run this analysis on a
# 6-concept domain, independent of SPoSE coverage.
# =============================================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(broom.mixed)
library(emmeans)
library(conflicted)
conflicts_prefer(dplyr::filter, dplyr::select, dplyr::lag, lmerTest::lmer,
                 .quiet = TRUE)

# Use the free version: 110 children against 32 in grid, and higher
# reliability in every domain (animals .27 vs .13, plants .24 vs .19). The grid
# version's by-age cells get as small as 3 children, which cannot support this.
VERSION <- "free"
N_PERM  <- 1000

# cor() errors rather than returning NA when a vector is entirely missing,
# which happens for every `conceptual` column in emotions (facial expressions
# have no SPoSE vector). Used anywhere a column may be all-NA for a domain.
safe_cor <- function(x, y, method = "pearson", min_n = 3) {
  ok <- is.finite(x) & is.finite(y)
  if (sum(ok) < min_n) return(NA_real_)
  if (sd(x[ok]) == 0 || sd(y[ok]) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  cor(x[ok], y[ok], method = method)
}

# Minimum age. Set to 5 for the robustness check described in the header: the
# 4-year-olds' single-trial reliability is .034, so their vectors carry almost
# no repeatable signal, and including them roughly doubles the spurious age
# slope. Report both.
AGE_MIN <- 4

set.seed(42)

# "avg" throughout: the Python script now groups picture sets by what the child
# saw in one trial (animals/plants [[1],[2]]; emotions [[1,2],[3,4]]), averages
# embeddings within a trial, and averages the resulting RDMs across trials --
# which is exactly what participant_dist_vecs() does to the child data. "all"
# (every exemplar pooled before distances) is available as a cross-check.
SET_CHOICE <- c(animals = "avg", plants = "avg", emotions = "avg")


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. LOAD AND ALIGN
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

rdms_raw <- read_csv("model_rdms_long.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

cat("\n--- what the builder produced ---\n")
rdms_raw %>% count(domain, model, picture_set) %>% print(n = Inf)

# Pick one picture_set per domain for the image models; SPoSE has none.
model_rdms <- rdms_raw %>%
  filter(model == "conceptual" |
           picture_set == SET_CHOICE[domain]) %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols    = c(domain, pair_index, concept_a, concept_b),
              names_from = model, values_from = distance) %>%
  arrange(domain, pair_index)

stopifnot("perceptual" %in% names(model_rdms))

cat("\n--- RDMs in use ---\n")
model_rdms %>%
  group_by(domain) %>%
  summarise(n_pairs     = n(),
            perceptual  = sum(!is.na(perceptual)),
            hybrid      = sum(!is.na(hybrid)),
            conceptual  = if ("conceptual" %in% names(model_rdms))
                            sum(!is.na(conceptual)) else 0L,
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  print()


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. VERIFY THE ELEMENT ORDER
#
# Everything below assumes element k of a child's dvec and row pair_index == k
# of model_rdms are the same pair of concepts. R's dist() stores the lower
# triangle column-major: (2,1),(3,1),...,(n,1),(3,2),... This reproduces that
# and compares it to what Python wrote. If it fails, STOP -- every correlation
# below would be quietly wrong, with no symptom.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

verify_pair_order <- function(rdms) {
  for (dom in unique(rdms$domain)) {
    d <- rdms %>% filter(domain == dom) %>% arrange(pair_index)
    concepts <- sort(unique(c(d$concept_a, d$concept_b)))
    n <- length(concepts)
    stopifnot(nrow(d) == n * (n - 1) / 2)
    lt <- which(lower.tri(matrix(0, n, n)), arr.ind = TRUE)   # column-major
    stopifnot(identical(concepts[lt[, "col"]], d$concept_a),
              identical(concepts[lt[, "row"]], d$concept_b))
  }
  cat("\nPair order verified against R's dist() for all domains.\n")
}
verify_pair_order(model_rdms)

# Second, independent check: the concepts the children saw are exactly the
# concepts in the RDMs, spelled the same way. A silent mismatch here is the
# most likely way for this whole analysis to produce plausible nonsense.
fp <- (if (VERSION == "free") final_placements_free else final_placements_grid) %>%
  filter(!is.na(category))     # tag_categories() leaves NA for unmatched names

concepts_child <- fp %>%
  distinct(category, base_name) %>%
  group_by(category) %>%
  summarise(child = list(sort(base_name)), .groups = "drop")

concepts_model <- model_rdms %>%
  group_by(category = domain) %>%
  summarise(model = list(sort(unique(c(concept_a, concept_b)))), .groups = "drop")

concept_check <- full_join(concepts_child, concepts_model, by = "category") %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(identical  = identical(child, model),
         only_child = paste(setdiff(child, model), collapse = ", "),
         only_model = paste(setdiff(model, child), collapse = ", ")) %>%
  ungroup()

cat("\n--- concept lists: children vs models ---\n")
concept_check %>% select(category, identical, only_child, only_model) %>% print()
if (any(!concept_check$identical, na.rm = TRUE))
  warning("Concept lists differ for at least one domain. Domains with a ",
          "mismatch are dropped below; fix ALIASES or the inventory.")

usable <- concept_check %>% filter(identical) %>% pull(category)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. HOW MUCH DO THE REFERENCES OVERLAP?
#
# Read this before any result below. Where perceptual and conceptual are highly
# correlated with each other, the unique shares are small and the design has
# little to work with -- that is a property of the stimuli, not of the children.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

if (!"conceptual" %in% names(model_rdms)) model_rdms$conceptual <- NA_real_

cat("\n--- correlations among the reference RDMs, by domain ---\n")
cat("(NA in a conceptual column = no SPoSE vectors for that domain)\n")
model_rdms %>%
  filter(domain %in% usable) %>%
  group_by(domain) %>%
  summarise(
    n_pairs     = n(),
    r_perc_hybr = round(safe_cor(perceptual, hybrid), 2),
    r_perc_conc = round(safe_cor(perceptual, conceptual), 2),
    r_conc_hybr = round(safe_cor(conceptual, hybrid), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  print()
cat("Where r_perc_conc is high, the two references are near-redundant and the\n",
    "unique shares will be small -- a property of the stimuli, not the children.\n")


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. CORRELATE EACH CHILD WITH EACH REFERENCE
#
# Spearman, because a child's placement distances are not linearly related to
# a cosine distance in an embedding space and there is no reason to expect them
# to be. Pearson is reported too, since the variance partitioning needs it.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

pdv <- participant_dist_vecs(fp) %>% filter(category %in% usable)

fit_one <- function(dvec, mods) {
  stopifnot(length(dvec) == nrow(mods))
  d <- tibble(y = as.numeric(dvec),
              p = mods$perceptual,
              h = mods$hybrid,
              k = if ("conceptual" %in% names(mods)) mods$conceptual else NA_real_)

  r2 <- function(form) summary(lm(form, data = d))$r.squared
  has_k <- !all(is.na(d$k))

  out <- tibble(
    rho_perceptual = cor(d$y, d$p, method = "spearman"),
    rho_hybrid     = cor(d$y, d$h, method = "spearman"),
    r_perceptual   = cor(d$y, d$p),
    r_hybrid       = cor(d$y, d$h),
    r2_perceptual  = r2(y ~ p)
  )
  if (!has_k) {
    return(out %>% mutate(rho_conceptual = NA_real_, r_conceptual = NA_real_,
                          unique_perceptual = NA_real_,
                          unique_conceptual = NA_real_,
                          shared = NA_real_, r2_full = NA_real_))
  }

  r2_full <- r2(y ~ p + k); r2_p <- r2(y ~ p); r2_k <- r2(y ~ k)
  out %>% mutate(
    rho_conceptual    = cor(d$y, d$k, method = "spearman"),
    r_conceptual      = cor(d$y, d$k),
    # both unique shares are R-squared differences from adding a predictor, so
    # both are >= 0. `shared` can be negative -- that is suppression, not a
    # bug, and it should be reported rather than clamped.
    unique_perceptual = r2_full - r2_k,
    unique_conceptual = r2_full - r2_p,
    shared            = r2_p + r2_k - r2_full,
    r2_full           = r2_full
  )
}

fits <- pdv %>%
  mutate(res = map2(dvec, category, function(v, dom) {
    fit_one(v, model_rdms %>% filter(domain == dom) %>% arrange(pair_index))
  })) %>%
  select(-dvec) %>%
  unnest(res) %>%
  left_join(age_df, by = "participant_id") %>%
  filter(!is.na(age), age >= AGE_MIN) %>%
  mutate(age_c = age - 6.5)

cat("\n--- mean fit to each reference, by domain ---\n")
fits %>%
  group_by(category) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            across(c(rho_perceptual, rho_hybrid, rho_conceptual),
                   ~ round(mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE), 3)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  print()


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. IS THE RAW CORRELATION JUST RELIABILITY?
#
# The diagnostic that decides which DV you can report. If raw fit tracks a
# child's own test-retest reliability, the raw numbers are measuring noise.
# The share should not track it.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

rel <- consistency_all %>%
  filter(version == VERSION, !is.na(consistency)) %>%
  select(participant_id, category, reliability = consistency)

fits <- fits %>%
  left_join(rel, by = c("participant_id", "category")) %>%
  mutate(
    # Mostly attenuation-free: the reliability factor appears in both unique
    # shares and cancels in the ratio, leaving only finite-sample R-squared
    # bias, which pulls the value toward .5. Undefined when the model pair
    # explains essentially nothing, so those rows are dropped rather than
    # given a meaningless value.
    conceptual_share = if_else(
      unique_perceptual + unique_conceptual > 1e-6,
      unique_conceptual / (unique_perceptual + unique_conceptual),
      NA_real_
    )
  )

cat("\n--- does fit track reliability? ---\n")
fits %>%
  group_by(category) %>%
  summarise(
    n                   = sum(!is.na(reliability)),
    rel_vs_rho_perc     = round(safe_cor(reliability, rho_perceptual), 2),
    rel_vs_rho_conc     = round(safe_cor(reliability, rho_conceptual), 2),
    rel_vs_share        = round(safe_cor(reliability, conceptual_share), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  print()
cat("Expected: rel_vs_rho_* substantial and positive, rel_vs_share much\n",
    "smaller. The share is not fully immune -- shrinkage toward .5 is stronger\n",
    "at low reliability -- so a small positive rel_vs_share is normal. If it is\n",
    "as large as rel_vs_rho_*, the share is buying you nothing and the whole\n",
    "age analysis is measuring noise.\n")

cat("\n--- how many children have a usable share? ---\n")
fits %>%
  group_by(category) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), n_share = sum(!is.na(conceptual_share)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  print()


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. IS ANY OF THIS ABOVE CHANCE?
#
# Permute the CONCEPT LABELS of the model RDM, not the elements of the distance
# vector. Shuffling elements destroys the matrix structure and gives an
# anti-conservative null, because real distance matrices have constraints
# (triangle inequality, shared rows) that a shuffled vector does not.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

long_to_matrix <- function(d) {
  concepts <- sort(unique(c(d$concept_a, d$concept_b)))
  n <- length(concepts)
  m <- matrix(0, n, n, dimnames = list(concepts, concepts))
  ia <- match(d$concept_a, concepts); ib <- match(d$concept_b, concepts)
  m[cbind(ia, ib)] <- d$distance_col
  m[cbind(ib, ia)] <- d$distance_col
  m
}

# A permuted model vector: relabel the concepts, then re-read the lower
# triangle in R's dist() order.
permuted_vec <- function(m) {
  p <- sample(nrow(m))
  as.vector(as.dist(m[p, p]))
}

perm_null <- function(dom, model_col, n_perm = N_PERM) {
  d <- model_rdms %>% filter(domain == dom) %>% arrange(pair_index) %>%
    mutate(distance_col = .data[[model_col]])
  if (all(is.na(d$distance_col))) return(NULL)
  m <- long_to_matrix(d)

  kids <- pdv %>% filter(category == dom) %>% pull(dvec)
  obs  <- mean(map_dbl(kids, ~ cor(.x, as.vector(as.dist(m)),
                                   method = "spearman")))
  null <- replicate(n_perm, {
    v <- permuted_vec(m)
    mean(map_dbl(kids, ~ cor(.x, v, method = "spearman")))
  })
  tibble(domain = dom, model = model_col,
         observed = obs,
         null_mean = mean(null),
         null_p95  = unname(quantile(null, 0.95)),
         p_perm    = (1 + sum(null >= obs)) / (n_perm + 1))
}

cat("\n--- permutation test against relabelled model RDMs ---\n")
perm_tbl <- expand_grid(
  dom = usable,
  model_col = intersect(c("perceptual", "hybrid", "conceptual"),
                        names(model_rdms))
) %>%
  mutate(res = map2(dom, model_col, perm_null)) %>%
  pull(res) %>%
  compact() %>%
  bind_rows()

perm_tbl %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4))) %>% print(n = Inf)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. DOES THE BALANCE SHIFT WITH AGE?
#
# Primary test, fitted three ways so the artifact is visible rather than
# assumed away. None of the three is clean on its own; the question is whether
# the age slope survives all of them.
#
#   (1) plain          compare against the simulated artifact: +.031/year would
#                      be expected with NO real shift if the true balance is
#                      conceptual-leaning
#   (2) + reliability  removes ~20% of the artifact
#   (3) ages 5-8       removes ~45%, at the cost of ~20% of the sample
#
# A slope that is large in (1) and vanishes in (3) is reliability, not
# development. A slope that holds up in (3) is worth reporting.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

share_dat <- fits %>% filter(!is.na(conceptual_share))

slope_table <- function(dat, label, multi) {
  if (n_distinct(dat$participant_id) < 10) {
    cat("\n[", label, "] too few children\n"); return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  form <- if (multi) {
    conceptual_share ~ age_c * category + (1 | participant_id)
  } else {
    conceptual_share ~ age_c + (1 | participant_id)
  }
  m <- lmer(form, data = dat)
  cat("\n[", label, "]  n children =", n_distinct(dat$participant_id), "\n")
  if (multi) print(summary(emtrends(m, ~ category, var = "age_c"), infer = TRUE))
  else       print(round(summary(m)$coefficients, 4))
}

multi <- n_distinct(share_dat$category) > 1

if (multi) {
  cat("\n--- does the age slope differ by domain? ---\n")
  print(anova(
    lmer(conceptual_share ~ age_c + category + (1 | participant_id),
         data = share_dat, REML = FALSE),
    lmer(conceptual_share ~ age_c * category + (1 | participant_id),
         data = share_dat, REML = FALSE)))
}

cat("\n=== age slope on the conceptual share, three ways ===")
slope_table(share_dat, "1. plain", multi)

# NB: `x <- if (a) b` followed by `else` on the next line is a syntax error at
# top level in R -- the statement ends at the newline. Braces avoid it.
m_cov <- if (multi) {
  lmer(conceptual_share ~ age_c * category + reliability +
         (1 | participant_id), data = share_dat)
} else {
  lmer(conceptual_share ~ age_c + reliability + (1 | participant_id),
       data = share_dat)
}

cat("\n[ 2. + reliability covariate ]\n")
if (multi) {
  print(summary(emtrends(m_cov, ~ category, var = "age_c"), infer = TRUE))
} else {
  print(round(summary(m_cov)$coefficients, 4))
}

if (AGE_MIN < 5) {
  slope_table(share_dat %>% filter(age >= 5), "3. ages 5-8 only", multi)
} else {
  cat("\n[ 3. ages 5-8 only ] AGE_MIN is already", AGE_MIN,
      "-- set it to 4 to see version 1.\n")
}

cat("\nBenchmarks: artifact ~+.031/yr (all ages) or ~+.017/yr (5-8) if the\n",
    "true balance is constant and conceptual-leaning; detection threshold\n",
    "~.067/yr. And remember the shrinkage -- an observed mean share of .64\n",
    "corresponds to a true share near .80.\n")

# Secondary, on the raw correlations, WITH reliability as a covariate. Without
# that covariate this model cannot separate a developing representation from a
# child who simply sat still; with it the age term is the part not explained by
# becoming less noisy. Report both, and say which is which.
raw_long <- fits %>%
  select(participant_id, category, age_c, reliability,
         rho_perceptual, rho_conceptual) %>%
  pivot_longer(starts_with("rho_"), names_prefix = "rho_",
               names_to = "model_type", values_to = "rho") %>%
  filter(!is.na(rho)) %>%
  mutate(model_type = factor(model_type, levels = c("perceptual", "conceptual")))

cat("\n--- raw fit ~ age, no reliability covariate (inflated) ---\n")
print(summary(lmer(rho ~ age_c * model_type + category + (1 | participant_id),
                   data = raw_long))$coefficients)

cat("\n--- raw fit ~ age, reliability partialled out ---\n")
print(summary(lmer(rho ~ age_c * model_type + reliability + category +
                     (1 | participant_id), data = raw_long))$coefficients)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. THE DIAGNOSTIC-PAIR TEST
#
# The sharpest version of the question, because it does not depend on the
# partition at all. Find the pairs where the two references disagree most, then
# ask how close children actually placed them. "Looks alike, conceptually
# distant" should be placed near by younger children and farther by older ones.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

conc_domains <- model_rdms %>%
  filter(domain %in% usable, !is.na(conceptual)) %>%
  count(domain) %>% filter(n >= 10) %>% pull(domain)

if (length(conc_domains)) {

  diagnostic_pairs <- model_rdms %>%
    filter(domain %in% conc_domains, !is.na(conceptual)) %>%
    group_by(domain) %>%
    mutate(gap = as.numeric(scale(conceptual)) - as.numeric(scale(perceptual)),
           pair_type = case_when(
             gap >= quantile(gap, 0.90) ~ "looks alike, conceptually distant",
             gap <= quantile(gap, 0.10) ~ "conceptually close, looks different",
             TRUE                       ~ NA_character_)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    filter(!is.na(pair_type)) %>%
    mutate(pair_id = paste(domain, concept_a, concept_b, sep = "_"))

  cat("\n--- diagnostic pairs ---\n")
  print(diagnostic_pairs %>% count(domain, pair_type))
  cat("\nEyeball these; if they do not look sensible, the RDMs are wrong:\n")
  diagnostic_pairs %>%
    group_by(domain, pair_type) %>% slice_head(n = 4) %>% ungroup() %>%
    select(domain, pair_type, concept_a, concept_b) %>%
    print(n = 40)

  # z-scored within child x domain, so a child who used a corner of the canvas
  # is not treated as placing everything close together
  child_pairs <- pdv %>%
    mutate(pair_index = map(dvec, seq_along)) %>%
    unnest(c(dvec, pair_index)) %>%
    rename(placement_dist = dvec) %>%
    group_by(participant_id, category) %>%
    mutate(placement_z = as.numeric(scale(placement_dist))) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    inner_join(diagnostic_pairs %>%
                 select(domain, pair_index, pair_type, pair_id),
               by = c("category" = "domain", "pair_index")) %>%
    left_join(age_df, by = "participant_id") %>%
    filter(!is.na(age), age >= AGE_MIN) %>%
    mutate(age_c = age - 6.5, pair_type = factor(pair_type))

  m_pairs <- lmer(placement_z ~ age_c * pair_type +
                    (1 | participant_id) + (1 | pair_id), data = child_pairs)

  cat("\n--- age x pair_type ---\n")
  print(summary(m_pairs)$coefficients)
  print(summary(emtrends(m_pairs, ~ pair_type, var = "age_c"), infer = TRUE))
} else {
  cat("\n--- diagnostic-pair test skipped: no domain has a conceptual RDM ---\n")
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. PLOT
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

p1 <- share_dat %>%
  ggplot(aes(age, conceptual_share)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, colour = "#0F728B", fill = "#0F728B",
              alpha = 0.15) +
  facet_wrap(~ category) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 4:8) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)",
       y = "Conceptual share of explained variance",
       subtitle = "0.5 = perceptual and conceptual contribute equally") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

p2 <- raw_long %>%
  mutate(age_bin = floor(age_c + 6.5)) %>%
  group_by(category, model_type, age_bin) %>%
  summarise(m = mean(rho), se = sd(rho) / sqrt(n()), n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(age_bin, m, colour = model_type)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = m - se, ymax = m + se),
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.2)) +
  geom_line(position = position_dodge(width = 0.2)) +
  facet_wrap(~ category) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(perceptual = "#0F728B",
                                 conceptual = "#F1731D")) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Fit to reference (Spearman rho)", colour = NULL,
       subtitle = "Raw, so still attenuated by measurement noise") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

print(p1)
print(p2)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. SAVE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

write_csv(fits %>% select(-any_of("age_c")), paste0("model_fits_", VERSION, ".csv"))
write_csv(perm_tbl, paste0("model_perm_", VERSION, ".csv"))
cat("\nwrote model_fits_", VERSION, ".csv and model_perm_", VERSION, ".csv\n",
    sep = "")
```
